QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_25

question.text: Which of the following is NOT a statutory duty of the custodian to a Cat III AIF under Chapter 9?

answer.text: Safekeeping of securities of the fund.
Keeping custody of securities and goods received in delivery against physical settlement of commodity derivatives.
Reporting information regarding investments of the AIF as specified by SEBI.
Independently executing long-short trades on behalf of the AIF without Manager instruction.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 20(11) (Chapter 9.7.2) lists: (1) safekeeping, (2) physical-commodity custody for Cat III, (3) SEBI-specified reporting. The custodian does NOT execute trades independently — trade execution sits with the Investment Manager; custodian is a back-office/clearing-member role. The Trap: Options A, B, C are direct Regulation 20(11) duties. Option D blurs custodian and investment manager roles — a common novice error. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C lists these duties across tracks. VIII (Equity Derivatives) covers the exchange-clearing-member role which overlaps custodian duties. Manager's Pro-Tip: In the Custodian Agreement, spell out the escalation matrix for corporate-action mis-handling (missed rights issue, wrong DVP) — Chapter 9.7.2 emphasises 'proper responsibility fixation' for back-office functions.
